name: Strandvik Rib-Knit Turtleneck
description:
A fitted rib-knit turtleneck in a substantial merino-analog yarn. The knit is dense but not stiff — it moves with the body and holds heat without trapping it. The turtleneck sits high and folds over once, covering the lower jaw in profile. The fit through the torso is close without being restrictive, and the sleeves are cut long enough to pull over the knuckles. Strandvik makes this in cream, charcoal, and black, and that's it — they've never offered another colorway and they don't intend to.

Strandvik is a small Scandinavian-heritage label that's been producing out of the same address in the upper corridor for twenty years. Their catalog is eight items. They don't discount, they don't advertise, and they have a six-week lead time on orders. The turtleneck is their flagship and their most copied piece — you can find knockoffs at every price point, but the yarn quality and knit tension of the original is identifiable to anyone who knows what to look for.
what_it_says: You know what you like and you've found it. You are not interested in trends. You own three of these.
worn_by: anyone who has found their uniform and stopped looking
story_hooks: Strandvik's founder died last year and left the label to two children who have completely opposite visions for its future — one wants to scale, one wants to close it.
A character is wearing a cream Strandvik turtleneck when something goes badly wrong — the blood doesn't wash out, and they can't bring themselves to throw it away.
Someone at a Tier 4 event can identify everyone in the room wearing a real Strandvik versus a knockoff and uses this as a social sorting mechanism.

physical_description.visual_profile: A precisely engineered second skin — the turtleneck creates a sleek, columnar silhouette from jaw to hip. The high collar frames the face with architectural precision, folding once to create a subtle ribbed band across the lower jaw. The overall impression is understated luxury with utilitarian restraint; minimal but never austere.
physical_description.fit: Fitted through the torso with zero excess fabric; contours closely to the body without compression. Sleeves extend generously past the wrist, designed to pool slightly at the knuckles when arms hang at rest. The fit suggests confidence without aggression — a garment worn by people who've solved the problem of looking good and moved on to other concerns.
physical_description.primary_material: Merino-analog yarn — a proprietary synthetic blend engineered to replicate merino's thermal regulation and breathability. Dense, substantial weight; the knit sits somewhere between athletic and luxury tailoring.
physical_description.texture: Rib-knit structure creates a fine, repeated vertical texture across the entire garment. Surface is smooth to touch but visually alive with micro-pattern. The knit tension is tight enough to hold shape through years of wear without pilling or degradation. Runs cool to the skin initially, then warms to body temperature within minutes.
physical_description.color_scheme: Offered exclusively in three colorways: cream (off-white with warmth), charcoal (cool mid-grey), and black. No variation, no seasonal adjustments. Each color is matte with no sheen — the ribbed texture diffuses light evenly.
physical_description.closures: None — pulls over the head; the high collar self-supports without fastening.
distinctive_features: High folded turtleneck sits at jawline, creates signature silhouette
Sleeves cut long enough to cover knuckles when arms relaxed
Identical rib-knit pattern front and back, no differentiation
Strandvik woven label at side seam (small, discrete)
Zero visible seaming — seamless construction at shoulders and sides
Yarn weight and knit tension remain consistent across entire piece — hallmark of quality that distinguishes originals from copies
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury. The price point (Φ280-320 new) and deliberate scarcity signal affluence, but the aesthetic is anti-status. Worn by people wealthy enough to reject conspicuous consumption.
physical_description.cultural_context: This is the uniform of the self-determined — corpo architects who've transcended brand signaling, research scientists, small-business owners who see clothing as infrastructure. Popular among augmentation clinics and independent makers. Never appears in nightlife settings; always appears in spaces where people are *building* something. The fact that knockoffs exist at every price point means wearing the real thing signals either heritage knowledge or quiet wealth — often both.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. Original Strandvik pieces develop a subtle gloss on high-contact areas (elbows, collar fold, cuffs) after 2-3 years of regular wear. This patina is valued. Even heavily worn originals don't fray or pill; they simply settle into the body and never leave.
